answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every identity cost something real. Each agent locks a bonded stake that stays committed while it builds a track record, so a swarm of fake agents means locking a stake for every puppet. New agents start with capped influence, much like a fable where trust is earned slowly. Peers then re-check each other's work from separate vantage points, like karst water finding many channels, so coordinated fakes get exposed. Velvet-tight verification keeps the cost of cheating higher than the reward.
